title: Why Saturn's Rings Are Younger Than the Dinosaurs
description: Saturn's vast icy rings are only ten meters thick in most places and are slowly falling into the planet.

shots.narration: The Cassini spacecraft slipped into the clear space between Saturn and its rings, looking back at millions of icy particles drifting together in silence.
These bands of bright water ice reach farther across than the distance to our Moon, yet most parts are only ten meters thick.
Dinosaurs walked Earth before the rings existed, and gravity is already pulling their ice downward, washing them away into the planet below.
